questions.q: Which endpoint is the prototype pollution source in this lab?
o: GET /my-account, which reflects the profile HTML as JSON
POST /my-account/change-address, which merges JSON unsafely
POST /admin/jobs, which merges job names into Object.prototype
PUT /login, which merges credentials into the session object
questions.x: POST /my-account/change-address recursively merges the JSON body into a server-side object. A __proto__ key makes that merge write onto Object.prototype. POST /admin/jobs is the later trigger, not the merge source.
questions.h: One endpoint updates billing JSON. The other starts workers. Which one performs the unsafe merge?

questions.q: How did the writeup confirm Object.prototype was writable before RCE?
o: A Burp Collaborator ping from the login JSON body
Express JSON came back indented after json spaces:10
The /admin panel listed extra keys on every job object
A debug route dumped Node heap strings after the merge
questions.x: The probe was __proto__ with json spaces set to 10. Express reads that option when it stringifies JSON, so the change-address response arrives pretty-printed with 10-space indent. That side effect proves the prototype is polluted.
questions.h: You want a harmless, visible change in HTTP JSON. Which Express formatting option controls indentation?

questions.q: Which Node.js function is the RCE gadget, and what inherited option does it read?
o: exec() reading a command string from Object.prototype.shell
fork() reading execArgv from Object.prototype on older Node
spawn() reading the executable path from Object.prototype.env._
require() loading a module path from Object.prototype.main
questions.x: POST /admin/jobs calls child_process.fork() with options that have no own execArgv. On Node before 18.18.0 or 20.6.0, fork() looks up execArgv through the prototype chain, so a polluted Object.prototype.execArgv becomes child CLI flags.
questions.h: The gadget is not shell or env._. Which child_process API starts a new Node worker, and which option holds Node CLI flags?

questions.q: What property was polluted for RCE, and what value made the child run code?
o: shell set to true, so every spawn call runs through /bin/sh
execArgv set to --eval=..., so the forked child runs attacker JS
env._ set to a command path that replaces the child executable
argv set to a crafted array that Node treats as the script name
questions.x: The payload sets Object.prototype.execArgv to an array whose entry is --eval= plus JavaScript. The child Node process runs that --eval during startup. From there execSync can delete /home/carlos/morale.txt. This is not a shell or env._ gadget.
questions.h: fork() forwards Node CLI flags. Which flag runs JavaScript immediately, and which prototype property carries those flags?

questions.q: On which Node versions does inherited execArgv work without copying it onto options?
o: Every current Node LTS release, including the latest 22.x line
Node before 18.18.0 or 20.6.0, where fork() followed prototypes
Only Node 4.x, when child_process still used the eval option
Only Windows Node builds that still honor inherited execArgv
questions.x: Until 18.18.0 and 20.6.0, child_process read option fields with a normal prototype lookup. After those releases it only honors own properties, so inherited Object.prototype.execArgv is ignored unless app code copies it first.
questions.h: A Node security fix stopped fork() from reading options off the prototype. Which version cutoffs does the writeup name?

questions.q: Which endpoint triggers the gadget after Object.prototype is polluted?
o: GET /admin, which renders the jobs table in the dashboard HTML
POST /admin/jobs, which forks Node workers for maintenance jobs
POST /my-account/change-address, which forks a worker per save
GET /login, which spawns a worker to validate the CSRF cookie
questions.x: Pollution is stored on the process by change-address. RCE happens when POST /admin/jobs forks workers. Those children inherit execArgv from Object.prototype and run the injected --eval.
questions.h: The merge endpoint pollutes. Which admin action starts the child processes that read execArgv?

questions.q: What merge mistake lets a __proto__ key pollute Object.prototype?
o: JSON.parse without a reviver copies keys onto Object.prototype
A recursive merge follows __proto__ and writes to the prototype
Storing the address in a Map automatically pollutes prototypes
eval of the JSON body assigns each key onto Object.prototype
questions.x: The merge walks attacker keys and recurses when the value is an object. Reading target["__proto__"] returns Object.prototype, so the next assignments write json spaces or execArgv onto the shared prototype.
questions.h: A recursive merge wants to update nested fields. What happens when the nested key it follows is __proto__?

questions.q: Which file must the RCE delete to solve the lab?
o: /var/www/html/app/index.js
/home/carlos/morale.txt
/tmp/node_modules/.bin/fork
/opt/express/json-spaces.conf
questions.x: The objective is to delete /home/carlos/morale.txt. The writeup first proves the gadget with sleep 5 via --eval, then swaps that command for rm of the morale file and triggers POST /admin/jobs again.
questions.h: The lab description names a file under the carlos home directory.

questions.q: Which of these statements about this prototype pollution lab is correct?
o: Change-address is the pollution source
Admin jobs is the pollution source
Old Node fork() ignores inherited execArgv
All of these statements are true
questions.x: POST /my-account/change-address is the unsafe merge that pollutes Object.prototype. POST /admin/jobs is the fork() trigger, not the pollution source. On Node before 18.18.0 or 20.6.0, fork() honors inherited execArgv. All is wrong because those last two claims are false.
questions.h: Which endpoint merges attacker JSON, and which one later forks the workers?

questions.q: Which of these statements about the RCE payload is correct?
o: The gadget pollutes shell for spawn()
The gadget overwrites env._ as the binary
json spaces:10 is the RCE payload itself
None of these statements are true
questions.x: The RCE gadget is execArgv plus --eval, not shell and not env._. json spaces:10 is only the confirmation probe that makes Express indent JSON. Command execution starts later, when admin jobs forks a child.
questions.h: Did this lab pollute shell or env._? Is the indented JSON probe the same thing as the --eval payload?
